source.title: Probing the Representational Power of Sparse Autoencoders in Vision Models
source.authors: M. Olson; M. Hinck; Neale Ratzlaff; Chang-Bai Li; Phillip Howard; Vasudev Lal; Shao-Yen Tseng

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature analysis to LLaVA, a multimodal model, and reports results on cross-modal feature overlap and visual representations across layers. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The LLaVA experiments bear on V4. The paper's DINOv2 OOD and ontology results and diffusion steering results concern other applications and are not rows for these claim versions. No experiment measures feature-over-dimension capacity, near-orthogonal geometry, or sparsity-dependent transitions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses SAEs as a tool on vision models and reports how well they work: OOD accuracy, ontology coverage, diffusion steering, and qualitative LLaVA probes. It never measures whether the model spreads features across neurons or whether SAEs recover the model's sparse features, beyond assuming they do. The LLaVA results concern cross-modal overlap and persistence across layers, a related but different construct from V4. The DINOv2 work is on a vision encoder, not an LLM.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that SAE features are semantically meaningful across vision encoders, LMMs and diffusion models. In vision encoders, they help OOD generalization and recover hierarchical (WordNet) structure. In diffusion models, they enable semantic steering. The LLaVA results are preliminary and qualitative, yet the conclusion states that shared vision-language representations are an emergent property of LLMs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses trained sparse autoencoders to analyze vision and multimodal representations, rather than training toy networks to test feature superposition and its geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The LLaVA visual-activation comparison varies representation point (projector output versus layer 6); the deeper point shows additional activated patches.

fits_no_version.finding: In DINOv2, across all 40 layers, 479 SAE features have ontological coverage above 0.99, versus 0 for the 61,440 original encoder neurons and 6 for random vectors (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In vision encoders, SAE features capture superordinate concepts that individual neurons do not. This is analogous to V4, but in a non-LLM vision model.

fits_no_version.finding: In LLaVA 1.5, the top 1% of SAE features overlap between text and image inputs for the same concept, and visual activations persist from the projector to layer 6 (qualitative only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multimodal LLMs share SAE-identified features across vision and language modalities.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
record.problems: The claim-relevant LLaVA findings are qualitative, with no numerical overlap measure or uncertainty estimate; the authors themselves describe them as preliminary and requiring future quantitative validation. The number of examined classes and images is not stated in the relevant results.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry, or sparsity transition.
No test of capacity or feature importance.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
No LLM measurement of features spread across neurons or of SAE recovery fidelity. The LLaVA probes take SAE features as given.
No test of completeness, stability, or canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. The LLaVA probes assume SAE features are meaningful and measure cross-modal sharing, not superposition or dictionary recovery in LLMs. The DINOv2 Table 2 comparison against neurons is the closest to V4, but it concerns a vision encoder. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, their geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The LLaVA results are qualitative; they do not quantify feature distribution across neurons or establish how completely SAEs recover the model's representations.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Does not test whether the underlying model features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: LLaVA 1.5
rows.operation_detail: Trained a ReLU SAE on middle-layer activations and compared the top 1% activated features for text and image representations of the same ImageNet concepts.

conditions.value: text-only definition versus image input followed by a description request

rows.measure: Overlap of activated SAE features across text and image representations
rows.value: The paper reports large overlap and says similar SAE features activate for nearly all examined classes; no numerical overlap values are stated in the text.
rows.note: The result is described qualitatively; Figure 6 presents the class-wise visualization.
rows.check: Measures overlap of SAE features across text and image inputs, a question of cross-modal alignment. It presupposes SAE features rather than testing whether the LLM holds sparse features in superposition. There is no baseline, and the overlap is not quantified.

rows.subject: LLaVA 1.5
rows.operation_detail: Trained SAEs at projector output and LLM layer 6, then compared image-patch activation maps.
rows.measure: Qualitative persistence of activated image regions across representation points
rows.value: Core activated regions remain consistent from projector output to layer 6, while layer 6 activates additional patches.
rows.note: The paper says this pattern was observed across multiple images but gives no count or quantitative measure.
rows.check: Measures whether visual activation maps persist from the projector to layer 6. This is about how representations evolve, not about superposition or dictionary recovery. It is qualitative, with no baseline or count of images.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LLaVA 1.5, text and image processing of the same concepts
reader_labels.reason: The authors report qualitative cross-modal overlap among activated SAE features and persistence of visual activations across early representation points (r1, r2).
